Oblique s/p incidence on a Lorentz-dispersive slab Measure complex r/t, power fractions and direct dissipation from actual finite-pulse evolutions and compare them with complex Fresnel slab references. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Use a two-dimensional field restricted to periodic transverse wave number ky = 4 and c = 1. The slab [4, 5] has epsilon_inf = 1.5, delta_epsilon = 0.75, omega_0 = 9, gamma = 0.5 and sigma = 0.04. Outer vacuum ends at PEC caps [-24, 36]; T = 60. Editorial clarification This is a genuine single-ky restriction rather than arbitrary transverse data. It covers one passive Lorentz pole and a fixed finite band/window. Gaussian tails are nonzero; window diagnostics and reference errors are reported separately. No strict all-frequency no-return proof is claimed. One transverse y period is shown. The displayed x and y scales differ to make the fields visible. Adopted numerical method Use the single-ky Yee spatial operator and local implicit-midpoint Lorentz ADE. Couple both p-polarized electric components to polarization, and remove incident propagation with a matched vacuum pulse on the same grid.
